tasks.title: Scaffold Next.js static-export app with G tokens, Geist fonts, and legacy preservation
tasks.description:
Replace the CRA app with a fresh Next.js App Router app using static export (output: 'export'), TypeScript, a unit test runner (Vitest + Testing Library), and lint. Rebuild from scratch, do not port CRA code.

Order matters:
1. BEFORE deleting any CRA code: create `git tag v1-legacy master` and `git branch legacy/cra-site master` locally (they are pushed by a follow-up). Copy src/assets/about/profile-round.jpg (300x300) into the new app's public assets. Record reusable site constants in `src/content/site.ts`: email ericlingren@gmail.com, GitHub and LinkedIn URLs (read from the old CRA source), mailto subject 'Hello from ericlingren.com', resume path constant `/eric-lingren-resume.pdf`. Do NOT carry over the old Inventory Manager demo login, myfxbook links, the localhost link, or the malformed Flickr OG image.
2. Remove CRA code and dependencies (react-scripts, react-router, gsap, tsparticles and similar old deps). No R3F, drei, WebGL, or detect-gpu.
3. Add global CSS with the theme tokens as custom properties: --po-bg #0c0a0e, --po-surface #111827, --po-ink #f9fafb, --po-muted #9ca3af, --po-border #252a36, --po-border-strong #3a4150, --accent #ff5a36, --accent-2 #06b6d4, --on-accent #0c0a0e, --sk-bg #eff1f4, --sk-line #1f2937, --sk-ink #111827, --sk-grid rgba(31,41,55,.11), --sk-hatch rgba(8,145,178,.28), --accent-ink-sk #bd4328. Add a build-line utility: linear-gradient(90deg, #ff5a36, #06b6d4) with 0 0 18px 2px coral glow. Dark only, no theme toggle.
4. Load Geist (headings and body) and Geist Mono via next/font. Both sketch and polished layers use the same fonts and sizes.
5. Add netlify.toml (build command, publish dir `out`) so Netlify keeps serving ericlingren.com. Add `.gitignore` entries for out/, .next/, node_modules/ (docs/private/ is already ignored).
6. Home page renders a minimal static placeholder (name as h1) so the pipeline is demoable.

Tests: a token test asserting every custom property above exists in the global CSS with the exact value, a contrast test asserting coral and cyan text pass 4.5:1 on --po-bg and --po-surface and #bd4328 passes on --sk-bg, and a render test for the home page. `next build` must produce `out/index.html`.
acceptance_criteria: Unit test asserts every theme token exists with its exact seed value
Unit test asserts accent text contrast >= 4.5:1 on each background it sits on (coral on obsidian and gray-900, cyan on obsidian and gray-900, #bd4328 on paper)
Render test passes for the placeholder home page and `next build` emits out/index.html
`git tag -l v1-legacy` and `git branch --list legacy/cra-site` both exist locally and point at master's tip
No react-scripts, react-router, gsap, tsparticles, three, or @react-three/* remain in package.json
src/content/site.ts exports email, GitHub URL, LinkedIn URL, mailto subject and resume path; profile-round.jpg exists in public assets

tasks.summary: Replaced CRA with Next.js 16 App Router static export (TS, Vitest + Testing Library, ESLint flat config, Geist via geist package). Theme tokens, build-line utility, site.ts, netlify.toml publishing out/, placeholder home h1. v1-legacy and legacy/cra-site created locally at master tip. tasks.title: Dual-layer Panel primitive and Hero panel on a flat page
tasks.description:
Build the Panel primitive that every section uses. A Panel renders its section content twice with an identical layout: a sketch layer (cool paper blueprint: --sk-bg paper, dashed --sk-line lines, --sk-ink text, 24px --sk-grid, image placeholders drawn as hatched X boxes using --sk-hatch) and a polished layer (obsidian/gray-900 palette). Layout parity rule: any CSS rule that changes layout applies to both layers; border widths stay identical (1.5px, solid in polished vs dashed in sketch); only color, background, border color, and border style differ. Coplanar layers get a 1px translateZ offset to avoid z-fighting. Each panel shows a Geist Mono component tag in cyan with its z position (for example `<Hero /> z=0`). Sketch layers can carry redline notes in Geist Mono using #bd4328, absolutely positioned so they never affect layout.

Also build the Hero panel in this primitive. Eyebrow 'FRONTEND-FIRST FULL-STACK ENGINEER' (hyphenated exactly, Geist Mono 500 at 13px, +0.14em tracking, coral). Headline is the name 'Eric Lingren' on two lines, clamp(52px, 10vw, 136px), line-height 0.92, Geist 600, -0.035em tracking, no gradient text. No punchy line under the name (parked; leave no placeholder text). CTAs: 'View work' (coral fill, #0c0a0e text) linking to the #work anchor, and an email button (cyan outline and text) using the shared mailto helper from src/content/site.ts with subject 'Hello from ericlingren.com'. Photo is NOT in the hero.

Render the home page as a flat stack of panels (polished layer only, sketch layer absent) with the Hero as the first. Content must be static HTML painted with no motion JS and no blocking preloader. Characterization is not needed (new code), but tests come first.

Tests: layout-parity test that renders both layers and asserts identical box geometry for the panel children (same computed width/height/border-width), a test that the eyebrow text matches exactly, a test that the 'View work' link targets #work and the email link href is `mailto:ericlingren@gmail.com?subject=Hello%20from%20ericlingren.com`, and a test that no element in the Hero contains profile image.
acceptance_criteria: Layout-parity test: sketch and polished layers render identical geometry and border widths for a sample panel
Test asserts eyebrow text is exactly 'FRONTEND-FIRST FULL-STACK ENGINEER'
Test asserts email CTA href equals mailto:ericlingren@gmail.com with subject 'Hello from ericlingren.com'
Test asserts 'View work' links to #work and the hero contains no photo
Sketch redline notes are position:absolute and a test asserts adding one does not change sibling layout
Page HTML contains the hero text with JavaScript disabled

tasks.title: Fly-through stage: 7-panel registry, camera, scroll mapping, and mouse look-around
tasks.description:
Add the fly-through stage as a client enhancement loaded AFTER first paint (dynamic import), so the flat static content paints first. Create a panel registry of 7 entries in order: Hero, Positioning, AI toolkit, Selected work, Experience, Testimonials, Contact. Panels not yet built render a minimal stand-in inside the Panel primitive (component tag plus title) so later tasks replace stand-ins one by one. Anchors/ids: hero, positioning, ai-toolkit, work, experience, testimonials, contact.

Stage mechanics (tunable constants in one config module): fixed full-viewport stage with perspective around 1100px containing a preserve-3d world; panel i at z = -i * D with D around 1700px; panels alternate horizontal offsets and a yaw that eases to 0 on arrival; the camera lerps toward scrollProgress * (N - 1) * D in a plain requestAnimationFrame loop; camera X follows a smoothstep between neighboring panel offsets; panels fade out shortly after the camera passes them. When the camera reaches a panel, it sits flat at z=0 and reads like a normal page. The world contains only panels and small annotations, never large planes such as a floor grid (Chrome depth sorting breaks). Motion is purely a function of scroll position, so scrolling up exactly reverses it.

Scroll spacer and sizing use stable viewport units (svh/lvh); do not read layout (offsetHeight etc.) on scroll or on Safari address-bar resize events. Panels scale down below about 1240px viewport width, with flatter yaw and smaller offsets on narrow screens.

Desktop only: a subtle mouse look-around (a few degrees of world rotation following the cursor). Touch devices get scroll only: no gyroscope, no DeviceOrientation listeners.

Keep all content real DOM in reading order. Put pure math (scroll progress to camera z, smoothstep X, yaw easing, fade) in a tested pure module.

Tests: unit tests for the pure camera math (monotonic, camera z at panel i equals -i*D at progress i/(N-1), yaw is 0 on arrival, fade bounds); a reversibility test that sampling progress p then going back to p yields identical transforms; a test that the touch path registers no deviceorientation listener and no mousemove look-around; a test that the fly-through module is not part of the initial HTML bundle.
acceptance_criteria: Pure camera-math unit tests pass, including exact camera z at each panel and yaw 0 on arrival
Reversibility test: transform at progress p is identical whether reached scrolling down or up
Test asserts no deviceorientation/devicemotion listener is registered on touch devices
Fly-through code is dynamically imported after first paint; initial HTML still contains all 7 panel titles
No offsetHeight/getBoundingClientRect read inside scroll or resize handlers (lint or test)
Registry has exactly 7 panels in the seed order

browser_verify.expected_visual_change: Home page now shows the Hero floating in a 3D stage with later panels receding in depth

tasks.summary: Fly-through stage: 7-panel registry with stand-ins (src/components/flythrough/registry.tsx, entries {id,name,title,render(z)}), pure camera math (camera.ts), tunable config.ts, rAF FlyStage, desktop-only mouse look-around (look.ts). Dynamically imported after first paint over a flat SSR stack carrying all 7 titles. Browser check skipped.

tasks.title: Per-panel build wipe, coral-to-cyan build line, and 1-bit dither band
tasks.description:
Drive fidelity progression per panel from camera distance: the sketch layer is wiped away from the top as the camera approaches, revealing the polished layer, with a visible build line at the wipe edge. Use the transform-only method: the sketch layer sits in an overflow-hidden box translated down by the built amount while its inner content is translated back up by the same amount. The build line and dither band ride the same translateY. Do NOT write clip-path per frame (repaints; measured 59fps vs 60fps with worse tail on the phone). Do not crossfade opacity (looks muddy gray).

Build line: coral-to-cyan horizontal gradient (linear-gradient(90deg, #ff5a36, #06b6d4)) with a 0 0 18px 2px coral glow. Dither band: a thin 1-bit coral band riding the build line, implemented in CSS without WebGL (for example a Bayer-pattern mask on a band element at the wipe edge). It must be stable and must not shimmer during motion; keep it on the compositor (transform only, no per-frame mask changes). Card hover glow (cyan border plus box-shadow 0 0 0 1px #06b6d4 and 0 0 28px at 40% cyan, 0.2s) applies to the polished layer only and is desktop hover only.

The built amount comes from a pure function of camera distance to the panel, clamped 0..1, fully built when the camera arrives at z=0.

Tests: unit tests for the pure built-amount function (0 far away, 1 at arrival, monotonic, symmetric on reverse); a DOM test that outer translateY and inner translateY are equal and opposite for several built amounts; a test that the wipe code never assigns clip-path or opacity per frame; a test that the dither band uses only transform for motion.
acceptance_criteria: Built-amount function unit tests: 0 at distance, 1 at arrival, monotonic, clamped
DOM test: sketch box translateY and inner counter-translateY sum to zero for sampled amounts
Test/lint asserts no per-frame clip-path or opacity writes in the wipe code
Dither band renders with no WebGL/canvas and moves via transform only
Build line uses the coral-to-cyan gradient and glow tokens

browser_verify.expected_visual_change: Hero shows a coral-to-cyan build line with a dither band wiping a paper wireframe into the polished obsidian layer

tasks.summary: Per-panel transform-only build wipe: inside the stage Panel renders polished layer plus overflow-hidden sketch box translated down by built amount with inner content counter-translated (no clip-path, no opacity). Coral-to-cyan build line and static CSS dither bands ride the same translateY. wipe.ts pure built-amount fn, stage-context.ts. Browser check skipped.

tasks.title: Flat fallback: Classic view, reduced motion, and frame-rate downgrade
tasks.description:
Add the flat stacked fallback: the same panel components rendered once, stacked, in polished mode only (no sketch layer, no 3D). It serves three triggers: `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the Classic view via `?view=classic` (shareable as ericlingren.com/?view=classic), and any device downgraded for poor frame rate. One flat component tree is shared by all three. This replaces the old three GPU tiers.

Frame-rate downgrade: a lightweight monitor samples frame times during the first seconds of fly-through and, when sustained frame rate is poor, switches to the flat page. Expose the monitor's live fps and frame-time readout under `?debug=perf` as a small unobtrusive overlay, so the phone can be checked with real touch input later.

Panels must support a 'complete' render mode (used by flat pages) so components like the AI diagram can show all steps complete instead of scroll-stepped; define the prop contract now and default new panels to it.

The mode is decided before the fly-through bundle loads so reduced-motion and Classic users never download it. No JS is needed to see content.

Tests: mode-resolution unit tests (reduced motion beats default, ?view=classic, downgrade); a test that the flat tree renders without sketch layers or 3D transforms; a test that the fly-through module is not requested in Classic or reduced motion; monitor tests with synthetic frame-time sequences (good stays interactive, sustained bad downgrades, a single spike does not).
acceptance_criteria: Mode-resolution unit tests cover reduced-motion, ?view=classic, downgrade and default interactive
Flat tree test: no sketch layer and no preserve-3d transforms render
Test asserts the fly-through chunk is not requested in Classic or reduced-motion modes
Frame monitor tests: sustained poor frames downgrade, a single spike does not
?debug=perf shows an fps/frame-time overlay only when present
Panel 'complete' render-mode prop contract documented and used by flat tree

browser_verify.expected_visual_change: ?view=classic shows the same panels as a plain stacked page with no 3D motion

tasks.summary: Flat fallback shared by reduced motion, ?view=classic and frame-rate downgrade (mode.ts resolves before the stage chunk is imported; FlatStack.tsx). Render-mode contract in render-mode.ts: RenderMode 'complete'|'staged', RenderModeContext (default 'complete'), useRenderMode(); FlatStack provides 'complete', stage provides 'staged'; documented in Panel.tsx. tasks.description:
Add the site nav containing: section anchors (Positioning, AI toolkit, Work, Experience, Testimonials, Contact), a segmented 'Interactive | Classic' switch naming both states (neither reads as a downgrade), and a resume link to the shared resume path constant. The switch is driven by the `view` query param and toggling it reloads/resolves the mode via the same resolver as the flat fallback. In Interactive mode an anchor click scrolls to the scroll offset that puts the camera at that panel; in flat mode anchors scroll to the element id. Resume link is NOT moved elsewhere on Classic. Nav is keyboard operable with visible focus rings; switch uses accessible roles (radio group or pressed buttons).

tasks.title: MDX case study pipeline with content-check script
tasks.description:
Add the /work/:slug route family as real, deep-linkable, statically exported DOM (generateStaticParams) with MDX content under content/work/*.mdx and frontmatter: title, slug, role, timeline, stack[], outcomes[], cardOutcome (one-line), cardNumber (string or null), cardNumberLabel, thumbnail, and order. Page renders a summary box at the top (role, timeline, stack, headline outcomes) then the body with sections Context, Problem, My role, Key decisions, Impact, What I'd do next. Plain polished DOM, not in the fly-through, dark only. Body 18px, line-height 1.68, 720px column; pull quote with a coral rule on a gray-900 surface; meta strip on gray-900; links to proof in cyan. Include one clearly marked fixture study for tests that is excluded from production routes.

Also add `scripts/check-content.mjs` and npm script `content:check` (with `--strict`). It scans content/ and src/content/ and reports file:line for: unresolved `[ERIC:` markers (strict only fails on these), internal-link patterns (private github.com orgs other than Eric-Lingren, linear.app, notion.so, slack.com, localhost), phone-number patterns, 'myfxbook', required sections missing, word count outside 600-900 for case studies, missing summary frontmatter, and PR/file/line-count phrases in frontmatter (counts are only allowed in body text as scale context). Customer and colleague names are guarded by a git-ignored `docs/private/blocklist.txt` if present.

Tests (first): MDX route renders the fixture with summary box and all six sections; content-check unit tests with fixtures for each rule; non-strict mode warns on [ERIC:] markers, strict mode exits non-zero.

tasks.title: Accent text legibility
tasks.description:
Accent text legibility

Both accents pass 4.5:1 (coral 6.4:1, cyan 8.1:1 on obsidian), so this is a perceived-legibility issue, mostly on small mono accent text (11 to 13px eyebrow, tags, links). Options from the prototype: brighter text-only tints of each accent (as done for electric blue with #7fa1ff), heavier weight or larger size for small accent text, or accent fills with dark text in place of accent-colored text.
